documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: December admission records in (ED record and L&D discharge summary). Abruption at 31w1d confirmed by retroplacental clot at delivery; severe-range BP 160/110 with 3+ proteinuria, AST 70 / ALT 65, platelets 120K, creatinine 1.2: severe preeclampsia without HELLP. Vaginal delivery 12/2. ED record also documents amphetamine use several times during the pregnancy; social work saw her. She did not mention this when we spoke in December. Will raise it gently at the six-week visit next week. Our 12/11 labs normal.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Postpartum Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks out from the 12/2 delivery. Saw OB last week; she says that visit went fine. Baby out of the NICU before Christmas and home with her.

BP: home readings normal, no symptoms. Gum bump is gone, she noticed it was flat by New Year's.

We went over the hospital record together. I asked about the amphetamine use it mentions. She was quiet for a moment, then confirmed she used several times during the pregnancy and has not used at all since the delivery. Met with the hospital social worker and has their resource list. No use of other substances. Doesn't want a referral right now; open to checking in about it here. I said plainly that stimulants raise blood pressure and the risk of exactly what happened, without blame, and that we'll support her whatever she decides.

PHQ-9 4. Sleep broken with the baby, mood otherwise good. No thoughts of self-harm.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: well. BP and vitals as charted. Gingiva normal, no residual nodule. Heart regular, lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Pyogenic granuloma of pregnancy: resolved after delivery.
2. Stimulant (amphetamine) use during pregnancy, none since delivery. Counseled; will revisit at each visit. Resources reviewed again.
3. Two pregnancies with severe preeclampsia, plus gestational hypertension in the first. Normotensive off meds. Annual BP, lipids and A1c; earlier visit for any sustained home readings of 140/90 or above.
4. Physical in June.

medications.reason: patient stopped in March; no longer pregnant

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
30 y/o here for her yearly exam. Back at work since March, kids well. Feels good. Home BP checks normal.

Med reconciliation: she stopped the iron on her own in March, figuring she no longer needed it. Still takes the prenatal vitamin daily. Iron taken off the list today.

Substance use: no amphetamine or other drug use since delivery, she says, and she volunteered it before I asked. Glass of wine occasionally. Never smoker.

ROS: no headaches, vision change, chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, edema. Periods have returned. Gums fine.
PHQ-9: 2.

Exam: BP and vitals as charted. Well appearing. Oral exam normal, gingiva healthy. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without lesions. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

Health maintenance: cervical screening current with OB. Flu due this fall.

A/P
1. History of preeclampsia (two pregnancies, severe both times) and gestational hypertension in the first. Normotensive. Fasting lipids, A1c, CMP and CBC today. Reviewed again that this history raises her long-run risk of hypertension and heart disease; best defenses are the habits she already has and yearly checks here.
2. Stimulant use in pregnancy, in sustained abstinence by her report. Continue to check in.
3. Iron stopped. Hemoglobin was 11.4 in December; CBC today to confirm it has recovered.

Flu shot and BP check in October; physical next June.
